items.title: apps.gankdat.com/weava-alternative.html: a comparison page for burned Weava / Super Simple Highlighter users, linked from the landing and both listings
items.why: RESEARCH.md 2026-09-19: Weava (200k users, last update Feb 2024) reviews say 'no longer saves your highlights', 'no way to cancel', 'stole $240'; Super Simple Highlighter 'saved pages started to disappear'. Those users search 'weava alternative' / 'weava not saving highlights' and there is no page of ours answering it. STRATEGY §5: distribution beats features until the funnel converts — a static page is the cheapest channel we own (Search Console already indexes apps.gankdat.com). Page: side-by-side table (local storage, no account, $12 once vs $3.99–7.99/mo), one honest paragraph per rival, Markdown export, install buttons for Chrome and Firefox, the refund line. DONE 2026-09-30 (burn-down): packages/landing/site/weava-alternative.html — 11-row table (storage, account, price, survival of page changes, notes, search, export, PDF, where it runs, last update, cancelling), one honest paragraph per rival with the export-before-you-cancel advice, a 'what we don't do' list (no PDF, no sync), Chrome + Firefox install buttons, the buy link and refund line; canonical URL. Linked from index.html, highlightkeep.html (which also gained the live store buttons instead of 'listings in review'), LISTING.md and amo-metadata.json (the AMO copy rides the 0.1.1 sign; the CWS copy is the owner's action-013 dashboard visit). sitemap.xml + robots.txt added so Search Console lists the page. Proof read from Search Console at the day-30 mark.
items.proof: Search Console: ≥ 50 impressions or ≥ 5 clicks on the page in 30 days; any install attributed to it

items.title: Highlight PDFs opened in the browser (PDF.js viewer page with the same anchoring and library)
items.why: The most-asked gap in every rival's reviews (RESEARCH.md 2026-09-19: Weava 'PDF highlighting broken', Glasp iframe gaps). Real differentiator but a feature: behind the three distribution items above until the funnel shows any install. Needs a bundled PDF.js viewer page, per-file storage keyed by URL/hash, and the anchor model extended to page+offset. DONE 2026-10-01 (burn-down, 0.2.0): own PDF.js viewer page (legacy build for Chrome 116+), 'Highlight this PDF' in the popup for web PDFs (site permission once, viewer fetches the file), highlights stored under the PDF's URL so popup/library/export are unchanged, library links PDFs back into the viewer; e2e section 4 proves create/restore in Chromium; comparison page, listing texts and welcome page updated; file:// PDFs stay unsupported and are said so. Rides the open 0.1.1 handoff (now 0.2.0).
items.proof: a 'PDF' mention in a review or support mail; paid conversions after release vs before

items.title: Library backup (JSON) and restore from the library page — the whole store out to one file and back in, merged
items.why: Both rival camps' fear is data loss: Weava 'folders and highlights randomly disappearing' (chrome-stats last-100 rating 2.9, read 2026-10-04), Super Simple's own help page says highlights 'aren't sent anywhere, synced, or backed up … if they're lost, they really are lost'. Highlight Keep has Markdown export only (core/model.ts); a JSON backup/restore is the no-server answer and the move-to-another-computer path, and the restore UI is what import-super-simple-highlighter plugs into. Listing and comparison page gain a 'Backup & restore' line. DROPPED 2026-10-04 (same run, 20:50): wrong premise — the library page already has Backup (JSON) and Restore (src/library/library.ts) and every listing text, the comparison page and the welcome page say so; the research grep covered core/ only. The one real gap (restore replaces the store instead of merging) is folded into import-super-simple-highlighter.
items.proof: a review or support mail naming backup/restore, or the comparison-page row read by the day-30 review

items.title: Import a Super Simple Highlighter backup file into the library ('bring your highlights'), said on the listing and the comparison page
items.why: Super Simple Highlighter (200k users, local, free) documents a backup (beta) export holding every style and highlight location (dexterouslogic.com help, read 2026-10-04); its reviews say saved pages disappear and the help page admits no sync or backup. A refugee with that file can move across in one click — the only paid-vs-free argument we can make concrete. Build after library-backup-restore (same restore UI); first obtain a real backup file's layout (install the extension in the e2e Chromium, make two highlights, export) before writing the parser — never guess the format. Note 2026-10-04: Backup/Restore already exist on the library page but Restore calls replaceAll (wipes the current store) — build a pure merge (core, tested: newer page wins, highlights unioned by id) and use it for both Restore and this import, so a second machine's highlights survive.
items.proof: ≥ 1 import reported in a review or support mail within 60 days; installs after the listing line vs before
